query: What are the requirements for a valid Swiss contractual non-compete clause under contemporary case law?

decisions.title: BGE 4I 123
decisions.text: A non-compete clause is valid only if it is limited in time, geographical scope, and content. The restriction must be justified by a legitimate business interest and proportionate to the employee's activity.

decisions.title: BGE 5A 456
decisions.text: A non-compete that extends beyond two years is presumptively disproportionate unless the employee had access to true trade secrets. Short durations of 6-12 months are generally upheld.

decisions.title: BGE 6B 789
decisions.text: Non-compete clauses applying to all employees of a company, including lower-level staff without access to confidential information, are disproportionate and unenforceable. The clause must be tailored to the individual's role.

decisions.title: BGE 3I 101
decisions.text: A non-compete clause may be enforced against a former employee who used the former employer's client list to solicit business, even if the clause's temporal scope is moderate (1 year), provided the geographical scope is limited to the former employer's operational region.

decisions.title: BGE 2A 202
decisions.text: An exception to the general non-compete rule exists for senior executives who have access to strategic planning information. For such individuals, non-compete clauses of up to three years may be upheld if reasonably scoped.
